-71.88904,45.40327.name: Charles River Safety Assessment Canada - Sherbrooke
-71.88904,45.40327.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

102.83000,16.44000.name: GM papaya — unapproved virus-resistant plants in commercial orchards
102.83000,16.44000.desc: Unapproved virus-resistant papaya was found in commercial plantings in Thailand, having spread from a research station. Papaya is propagated and traded locally, so material moves through channels no register follows.

4.74800,51.62800.name: Protix
4.74800,51.62800.desc: Breeds black soldier fly larvae for feed at commercial scale, supplying fish and poultry producers across Europe. The EU approved insect protein in aquaculture feed in 2017 and in poultry and pig feed in 2021, which is how a novel organism enters the food chain without ever being described as one.

176.27000,-38.14500.name: Scion — gene-edited conifer programme
176.27000,-38.14500.desc: The same institute launched what it describes as the world's first field trial of a gene-edited conifer, using CRISPR to switch off single genes in the pine genome to study wood development, with two sets of trees each carrying a different gene turned off. Separately it has edited Douglas-fir reproductive genes to produce trees that grow normally but cannot reproduce — aimed at New Zealand's wilding conifer problem, where planted forest species spread beyond their plantations into native ecosystems. The proposal is that sterile trees could act as a form of biocontrol for future engineered trees. Note what that means: the answer to trees spreading is a tree engineered not to spread, which is the same reasoning the aquaculture facet uses for sterile fish, arrived at independently in a different kingdom.
